chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Which type of Hajj is superior?' He said: 'Al-Tamattu'. And how can anything be superior to it, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If I had faced from my affairs what I faced, I would have done what the people did.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know of a Hajj for Allah other than Al-Mut'ah. When we meet our Lord, we will say: 'Our Lord, we acted by Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet,' while the people will say: 'We acted by our own opinions.' So Allah will place us and them wherever He wills.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Al-Tamattu (Enjoyment), a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj separately with a break in between.
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Al-Mut'ah, often used interchangeably with Tamattu in this context, referring to the same ritual practice.
key_terms.رَأْيِنَا: Our opinions, referring to personal juristic reasoning or opinion (ra'y) as opposed to divine revelation.
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: The Sunnah of Your Prophet, referring to the established practices and traditions of Prophet Muhammad.

ai.seo_question: What is the best type of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes Al-Tamattu' as the superior form of Hajj, supported by the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) declaration that he would have chosen it if he could have foreseen his later circumstances. It highlights a key Shia theological distinction, contrasting the Ahl al-Bayt’s strict adherence to the Quran and Sunnah against the general populace’s reliance on personal opinion (ra'y), thereby affirming the authenticity of the Tamattu' practice in Shia jurisprudence.
